title: Symmetric blowup along the closure of one nodal point
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed] and $V\subseteq K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, meaning that for $z\in K^\times$ either $z$ or $z^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-curve here is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with pure one-dimensional fibres [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], without any separatedness or properness assumption. A curve is semistable if every nonsmooth point of every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $f:X\to S$ be a semistable $S$-curve with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $J=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega^1_{X/S})$ and $N=V_X(J)$, the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], and suppose its underlying set is finite. Fix any point $z\in N$, put $s_0=z|_S$, and let $C=\overline{\{z\}}\subseteq X$ be its topological closure. The set $C$ is contained in $|N|$. There exist a nonzero element $\pi\in V$, an open neighbourhood $W$ of all of $C$ in $X$, and a finite affine open cover $W=\bigcup_\alpha W_\alpha$ with the following properties. The vanishing set $V_S(\pi)$ is exactly the closure of $\{s_0\}$ in $S$, and $|N|\cap W\cap f^{-1}V_S(\pi)=C$. Each $W_\alpha$ maps into an open $S_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}R_\alpha$ of $S$, with $R_\alpha$ a localization of $V$. There are $0\ne a_\alpha\in R_\alpha$, an etale cover $T_\alpha\to W_\alpha$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and an etale $R_\alpha$-morphism $T_\alpha\to M_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}R_\alpha[u,v]/(uv-a_\alpha)$, such that $J\mathcal O_{T_\alpha}=(u,v)\mathcal O_{T_\alpha}$ and $b_\alpha=a_\alpha/\pi^2\in R_\alpha$. The ideals $J|_W+(\pi)$ on $W$ and $\mathcal O_{X\setminus C}$ on $X\setminus C$ agree on their overlap, so define a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$.
The blowup $q:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_I X\to X$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], is an isomorphism on $X\setminus C$ and on the whole generic fibre, and $X^+$ is a reduced semistable $S$-curve. The blowup is locally covered by the rings $A[I/g]\subseteq A_g$ for generators $g$ of $I$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Its pullback to $T_\alpha$ is the etale pullback of the blowup of $(u,v,\pi)$ on $M_\alpha$. The three standard chart rings of that model blowup are
$$R_\alpha[u,p]/(up-\pi),\qquad R_\alpha[r,t]/(rt-b_\alpha),\qquad R_\alpha[v,h]/(vh-\pi),$$
with maps to $M_\alpha$ given respectively by $v=\pi b_\alpha p$, by $u=\pi r,v=\pi t$, and by $u=\pi b_\alpha h$. For every $s\in S$, every reduced irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $(X^+)_s$ is smooth over $\kappa(s)$ at every point that maps into $C$. If $E\hookrightarrow X$ is any closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] disjoint from $C$, its inverse image is isomorphic to $E$.

source.place: Remark 4.5.2 (printed p. 33), strictification input; §4.3, Proposition 4.3.1 (printed pp. 27--28), nodal blowup chart calculations. Agent-reconstructed symmetric (u,v,pi) version along the whole closure of one node, using the etale node model of Stacks Tag 0CBY, curves.tex, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family. No claim that the source states this auxiliary lemma verbatim; local archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By the nodal Fitting theorem, $N$ is the closed nonsmooth locus and $N\to S$ is unramified; hence $C\subseteq|N|$ and $s_0\ne\eta$. The valuation ring and its localizations are normal domains. Apply 09Z9 to $S$: after taking affine neighbourhoods in any etale base neighbourhood, their maps to $S$ split into open immersions. Moreover $N\to S$ is locally on $N$ a closed immersion into an open of $S$. Indeed apply the finite-unramified-neighbourhood theorem to one point, replace its etale base by an open-immersion component containing the marked base point, and apply 04DG to its finite unramified piece with unique purely inseparable fibre point. Its open piece contains the original point. Thus every point of $N$ has an open neighbourhood in $N$ whose map to $S$ is injective, induces residue-field isomorphisms, and reflects specialization.

Put $F=|N|\cap f^{-1}(\overline{\{s_0\}})$. This is a finite closed subset of $X$. If $c\in C$ and $w\in F$ generalizes $c$, take the local immersion neighbourhood of $c$ obtained in step 1. It contains both $z$ and $w$. Their base points satisfy $s_0\leadsto f(w)$, since $f(w)$ is a specialization of $s_0$. A locally closed subspace reflects specialization, so $z\leadsto w$ and $w\in C$. Thus $C$ is both specialization-closed and generalization-closed in $F$. For every $w\in F\setminus C$, its closure in $X$ is contained in $F$ and misses $C$. Delete the union of these finitely many closures from $X$, obtaining an open $W^0$ containing all of $C$ with $F\cap W^0=C$. This uses no separatedness of $X$.

For every $c\in C$, apply 0CBY to $X/S$ at $c$. Its flatness, local finite presentation, pure dimension and geometric-node hypotheses are exactly the assumptions here. Restrict its etale base neighbourhood to an affine open and then to the component through the chosen point furnished by step 1; this is an open of $S$. Shrink it to $S_c=\operatorname{Spec}V_{f(c)}$. This is an open because the prime chain is finite: the set of primes contained in $f(c)$ is the complement of the closed set starting at the next prime. The etale source chart still contains a point over $c$. Its image in $X$ is open, by openness of flat locally finitely presented maps. Choose an affine open $W_c$ containing $c$ inside that image, inside $W^0$, and mapping into $S_c$. Its preimage $T_c$ in the chart is an etale surjective cover of $W_c$, with an etale $S_c$-map to $M_c=\operatorname{Spec}R_c[u,v]/(uv-a_c)$. Keep one such choice for each of the finitely many $c$. Set $W=\bigcup_c W_c$. Every $W_c$ contains $z$, because $z$ generalizes $c$.

On $M_c$ the universal derivation gives $\Omega_{M_c/R_c}=(A\,du\oplus A\,dv)/(v\,du+u\,dv)$: a derivation is precisely a pair satisfying this relation. The first minors of this presentation generate $(u,v)$. The affine etale criterion gives $H_1(L)=0$ and $\Omega=0$ for each etale chart map. Thus the formally-etale differential equivalence, followed by Fitting base change, identifies both pullbacks to $T_c$. Thus $J\mathcal O_{T_c}=(u,v)\mathcal O_{T_c}$. In particular, a lift of $z$ shows that $a_c$ vanishes at $s_0$. Also $a_c\ne0$. Otherwise the image of $T_c\to M_c$ is an open containing a point of the node section $u=v=0$, and therefore contains its generic point over $S_c$. A point of $T_{c,\eta}$ above that generic node has nonunit first Fitting ideal by this calculation. But $T_{c,\eta}\to X_\eta$ is etale and $X_\eta$ is smooth, whose first Fitting ideal is the unit ideal by the nodal Fitting theorem. This is a contradiction.

source.place: Direct universal differential presentation; affine etale criterion 02GJ (morphisms.tex, lemma-etale-characterize), differential base change 0H93, Fitting base change and nodal Fitting-locus theorem

proof.text:
Write $\mathfrak p_0$ for $s_0$, and let $\mathfrak p_-$ be the immediately preceding prime, which exists because $\mathfrak p_0
e0$. Choose $d\in\mathfrak p_0\setminus\mathfrak p_-$. Each $a_c\in V_{f(c)}$ actually lies in $\mathfrak p_0\subset V$: write $a_c=n/e$ with $e
otin f(c)\supseteq\mathfrak p_0$ and $n\in\mathfrak p_0$. If $n/e
otin V$, its inverse lies in $V$, forcing $e\in\mathfrak p_0$, a contradiction; primality then gives $n/e\in\mathfrak p_0$. In additive valuation notation choose $\gamma=\min(v(d),v(a_c):c\in C)$. It is achieved by an element $d_0\in\mathfrak p_0\setminus\mathfrak p_-$: a member of $\mathfrak p_-$ cannot have value at most $v(d)$. Divisibility of the value group gives $\pi\in K^	imes$ with $3v(\pi)=\gamma$. Then $\pi\in V$ and $\pi^3/d_0$ is a unit of $V$, so $\sqrt{(\pi)}=\sqrt{(d_0)}=\mathfrak p_0$, since no smaller prime contains $d_0$. Finally $v(a_c/\pi^2)\ge\gamma/3=v(\pi)$, so $b_c=a_c/\pi^2\in(\pi)V\subseteq\mathfrak p_0$. This stronger choice makes every $b_c$ vanish on $\overline{\{s_0\}}$.

source.place: Agent ordered-value-group calculation; divisibility supplied by the cited node

proof.text: By step 2 and $V_S(\pi)=\overline{\{s_0\}}$, the support of $\mathcal O_W/(J+(\pi))$ is precisely $C$. Thus $J+(\pi)$ is the unit ideal on $W\setminus C$ and glues with the unit ideal on $X\setminus C$. This constructs $I$ by equality of sheaves on the overlap. It is quasi-coherent because the Fitting ideals commute with localization, and finite type: locally write a finite presentation $B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ of $X/S$; its differential module has the finite presentation with generators $dx_i$ and the $m$ relations $dg_j$, so its first Fitting ideal has finitely many minors. Adjoining the generator $\pi$ preserves finite generation. Hence $I$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal without any Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Elementary finite presentation, minors and sheaf gluing

proof.text: Form $q=\operatorname{Bl}_I X\to X$. The global finite-type blowup theorem makes $q$ proper. Its complement theorem, applied to $V(I)=C$, makes $q$ an isomorphism over $X\setminus C$. Since $C$ misses $X_\eta$, this includes the whole generic fibre. For any closed subscheme $E\hookrightarrow X$ whose underlying set misses $C$, the morphism factors through the open $X\setminus C$; base change of that restricted isomorphism gives $q^{-1}(E)\simeq E$, with its full scheme structure.

source.place: Nagata blowup properness and complement nodes; final assertion is base change of an isomorphism

proof.text: Etale maps are flat. Apply the flat blowup comparison to $T_c\to W_c$ and to $T_c\to M_c$. The extended ideals on $T_c$ coincide, both being $(u,v,\pi)$ by step 4. Thus $X^+\times_XT_c$ identifies with $T_c\times_{M_c}\operatorname{Bl}_{(u,v,\pi)}M_c$. These are flat base changes, not blowup base change along a residue field. The affine-chart-cover theorem gives, for every affine presentation of $I$, the asserted cover by $A[I/g]\subseteq A_g$. In particular the model blowup is covered by the $u$, $\pi$ and $v$ charts.

source.place: Nagata flat blowup comparison and affine chart cover

proof.text: Fix a chart and omit its subscript. The domain $A=R[u,v]/(uv-a)$ embeds in $\operatorname{Frac}(R)[u,u^{-1}]$ via $v=a/u$, since every class has a unique normal form $c_0+\sum_{i>0}c_i u^i+\sum_{j>0}d_jv^j$; independence follows from distinct Laurent exponents and $a\ne0$. In $A_u$ set $p=\pi/u$. Then $v=\pi bp$ and $v/u=bp^2$, so the subalgebra generated by $A,v/u,\pi/u$ is generated by $u,p$ with relation $up=\pi$. The same normal-form argument, now with nonzero $\pi$, proves injectivity of $R[u,p]/(up-\pi)\to A_u$ and therefore identifies this ring with the actual $u$ blowup chart. Interchanging $u,v$ gives $R[v,h]/(vh-\pi)$ with $h=\pi/v$ and $u=\pi bh$. These are the subalgebra charts, so there is no extra torsion or exceptional component from an unsaturated presentation.

source.place: Agent Laurent normal-form calculation in the subalgebra definition of a blowup chart

proof.text: In $A_\pi$ set $r=u/\pi$, $t=v/\pi$. They generate the $\pi$ chart and satisfy $rt=b$. The map $R[r,t]/(rt-b)\to A_\pi$, $r\mapsto u/\pi$, $t\mapsto v/\pi$, is injective by the normal-form argument of step 9 ($b=a/\pi^2\ne0$); after embedding in $\operatorname{Frac}(R)[u,u^{-1}]$, its distinct positive and negative powers cannot cancel. It is surjective onto the generated chart algebra, since $u=\pi r$ and $v=\pi t$. This proves all three displayed chart rings and all the claimed maps to $M$.

source.place: Agent calculation of the pi chart and its saturation

proof.text: For each nonzero $e\in R$, the normal form in $R[x,y]/(xy-e)$ is the free $R$-basis $1,x,x^2,\ldots,y,y^2,\ldots$; hence it is flat and finitely presented over $R$. A geometric fibre is $\Omega[x,y]/(xy-\bar e)$. If $\bar e\ne0$ it is $\Omega[x,x^{-1}]$; if $\bar e=0$, it is the union of two affine lines, smooth off their intersection, with completed local ring $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$ there (both rings have the same quotients modulo every power of $(x,y)$). It is pure one-dimensional in either case. Apply nodal source locality first to the etale pullbacks of these three models, and then to the jointly surjective etale cover of $X^+$ consisting of those pullbacks and $X\setminus C$. On the latter open the original nodal family is unchanged. Thus $X^+\to S$ is flat, locally finitely presented, and has pure one-dimensional geometric nodal fibres.

The proper morphism $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; together with finite presentation of $X/S$, the qcqs permanence statements make $X^+/S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Combined with local finite presentation from step 11, this is finite presentation. For reducedness take a local ring $B$ of $X^+$. Flatness over its base valuation ring implies $B\hookrightarrow B\otimes_VK$: tensor the injections given by multiplication by each nonzero scalar, then localize. Its generic localization is reduced because $X^+_\eta\simeq X_\eta$ is smooth over a field and hence geometrically reduced. A nilpotent of $B$ therefore maps to zero in that localization and was already zero. This proves $X^+$ reduced, including away from the chosen charts.

source.place: Qcqs permanence; reducedness by flat injection into the reduced generic fibre

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and $x\in C\cap X_s$. Step 1 shows $\kappa(x)=\kappa(s)=k$: the local immersion of $N$ into $S$ has this property. In particular $x$ is closed in $X_s$ (in every affine neighbourhood it is a $k$-rational maximal ideal). The residue-field theorem also says $k$ is separably closed. Choose a chart lift $t\in T_c$ of $x$; its residue extension is finite separable, so it is $k$. The image in $M_c$ is its rational node $u=v=0$. Base change the isomorphism of schemes in step 8 further along $\operatorname{Spec}k\to T_c$. It identifies the entire fibre $q^{-1}(x)$ with the fibre of the computed model blowup over its node. This is base change of an already proved isomorphism, and does not assert blowup commutes with the nonflat map to $k$. Here $\pi(s)=b_c(s)=0$ by step 5.

source.place: Sepclosed residue fields; ordinary fibre of the flat-comparison isomorphism

proof.text: In this model fibre the $u$ chart is $k[p]$ ($u=0$), the middle chart is $k[r,t]/(rt)$, and the $v$ chart is $k[h]$ ($v=0$). On the overlap of the $u$ and middle charts, $p=1/r$ and $t=0$; on the middle/$v$ overlap, $h=1/t$ and $r=0$. The $u$/$v$ overlap is empty in this fibre. Thus the fibre is exactly two copies $L_u,L_v$ of $\mathbf P^1_k$, meeting only at $r=t=0$. These are distinct closed integral curves in $(X^+)_s$, since the fibre over the closed point $x$ is closed. Every fibre is a pure one-dimensional finite-type $k$-scheme by step 11, so each $L_u,L_v$ is a whole irreducible component: otherwise a closed point of $L_u$, then $L_u$, then a larger irreducible component would give a chain of length two, contradicting dimension one (and similarly for $L_v$). This explicitly distinguishes the two global components through the middle node.

source.place: Agent computation of exceptional fibre by the three affine overlaps

proof.text: The other possible nonsmooth points above $x$ are the endpoints $u=p=0$ and $v=h=0$ in the outer charts. At the first, the branch $u=0$ lies in $L_u$, whereas the branch $p=0$ is not contracted: the coordinate $u$ is nonconstant on it and maps to the original branch $v=0$. An etale chart preserves that nonconstancy. Hence these branches lie in different global fibre components. The second endpoint is the same calculation with $u,v$ exchanged. At the middle node they lie in $L_u,L_v$, already distinguished in step 14. The nodal fibre is geometrically reduced by the nodal reducedness theorem, and the separably-closed residue-field theorem identifies its reduced components with geometrically integral components. Etale base change preserves the reducedness of a reduced component, by the etale-reducedness theorem. Consequently, in an etale node chart a fixed reduced global component has exactly one of the two local branches at each of these three nodes: locally its pullback is the quotient by that branch ideal, $k[u,p]/(up,u)=k[p]$ or $k[u,p]/(up,p)=k[u]$, and similarly in the middle and right charts. It is smooth there; etale source locality of smoothness descends this to the component itself. At all other points over $x$ the fibre is already smooth and has just one local component. This proves the component assertion for every $x\in C_s$ and every $s$, even when a component of the original fibre has a self-node.

source.place: Agent branch separation argument; smoothness descent Tag 036U
